events.title: Avitus is acclaimed Western Roman Emperor near Arles
events.description: Backed by the Visigoths and the Gallo-Roman nobility, the senator Avitus was acclaimed emperor near Arles. His reign lasted barely a year, a sign of how weak the Western Empire had become.
events.html: Backed by the Visigoths and the Gallo-Roman nobility, the senator Avitus was acclaimed emperor near Arles. His reign lasted barely a year, a sign of how weak the Western Empire had become.

events.title: Silla defeats Baekje at the Battle of Hwangsanbeol
events.description: Near present-day Nonsan, a large Silla army under Kim Yu-sin destroyed a small Baekje force; its commander, General Gyebaek, was killed. With a Tang army landing at the same time, the Baekje capital Sabi fell within days, ending the kingdom.

events.title: Jawhar al-Siqilli leads the Friday prayer in Fustat
events.description: The Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli led the Friday prayer in Fustat in the name of Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah, symbolically completing the conquest of Egypt. The Fatimids then founded Cairo as their new capital, making Egypt the centre of their power.

events.title: The Swiss defeat Duke Leopold III of Austria at Sempach
events.description: Swiss Confederates defeated the army of Duke Leopold III of Austria near Sempach, in the canton of Lucerne, killing Leopold and many of his nobles. Together with the victory at Näfels in 1388, it confirmed the Confederacy's independence from Habsburg rule.

events.title: New Yorkers topple George III's statue after the Declaration is read
events.description: Washington had the Declaration read to his troops in New York. That evening a crowd pulled down the gilded lead statue of George III on Bowling Green; much of the lead was later cast into musket balls.

events.title: Napoleon annexes the Kingdom of Holland to France
events.description: Days after his brother Louis abdicated rather than enforce the blockade of British trade, Napoleon decreed Holland's annexation to the French Empire. Dutch independence was restored only in 1813.
events.html: Days after his brother Louis abdicated rather than enforce the blockade of British trade, Napoleon decreed Holland's annexation to the French Empire. Dutch independence was restored only in 1813.

events.title: The 14th Amendment wins enough states for ratification
events.description: South Carolina's and Louisiana's approval gave the 14th Amendment the three-quarters of states it needed. It guaranteed citizenship to all born in the US and equal protection of the laws.
events.html: South Carolina's and Louisiana's approval gave the 14th Amendment the three-quarters of states it needed. It guaranteed citizenship to all born in the US and equal protection of the laws.

events.title: The first Wimbledon Championships begin
events.description: The All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club opened its first lawn tennis championship, with 22 men competing. Spencer Gore won the title ten days later, launching the world's oldest tennis tournament.
events.html: The All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club opened its first lawn tennis championship, with 22 men competing. Spencer Gore won the title ten days later, launching the world's oldest tennis tournament.

events.title: South Sudan becomes independent
events.description: South Sudan declared independence from Sudan after a referendum, becoming the world's newest internationally recognised state. Independence followed decades of civil war, but a new conflict erupted in 2013.
